message.content: {"caption":"A 12-panel line chart of accuracy across six math benchmarks, three code benchmarks, and three aggregate averages, grouped into Math Reasoning, Code Reasoning, and Overall Performance.","description":"The target is a multi-panel line chart arranged in four rows of three. Each panel plots accuracy on its own vertical scale against horizontal tick values from 50 to 350; the horizontal axis has no printed label. The first six panels have blue lines and pale blue backgrounds and are grouped under “MATH REASONING”: AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 (top row, first and second) and Olympiad Bench (top row, third); Minerva, Math 500, and AMC 2023 (second row). AIME 2024 fluctuates widely at low accuracy and rises to its highest level near the right edge. AIME 2025 alternates between zero and higher values, with several peaks near 0.10. Olympiad Bench stays comparatively steady around 0.35–0.385. Minerva rises sharply from its low starting point, then fluctuates around 0.35–0.38. Math 500 trends upward overall to a peak around the mid-to-late x range, then falls near the end. AMC 2023 is highly variable, reaching about 0.60 near x=200, dropping to a trough below 0.40 near x=300, and recovering toward the end. The three orange-line panels under “CODE REASONING” are HumanEval+, MBPP+, and LiveCodeBench. HumanEval+ generally rises from about 0.82 toward 0.84–0.85 with fluctuations; MBPP+ oscillates around 0.69–0.71 and declines slightly at the end; LiveCodeBench generally rises from about 0.27 to above 0.31, with fluctuations. The bottom row under the green heading “OVERALL PERFORMANCE” contains Math Average, Code Average, and Overall Average. Math Average varies but trends upward overall, with a late high; Code Average rises gradually from about 0.59 to around 0.62 before a small late dip; Overall Average rises from about 0.455 toward 0.50. A red star marks a point near the upper-right end of the Overall Average panel. Pale fills and gridlines appear behind the lines.
